sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界，并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的瑞秋·艾布拉姆斯，这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: It's been nearly two years since Hamas carried out its deadly attacks on Israel on October 7th and Israel began its bombardment of Gaza.
sentences.zh: 哈马斯于10月7日对以色列发动致命袭击，随后以色列开始轰炸加沙，至今已近两年。

sentences.en: Since then, the humanitarian crisis in Gaza has only worsened.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，加沙的人道主义危机只会愈演愈烈。

sentences.en: And Hamas is still holding hostages.
sentences.zh: 而且哈马斯仍扣押着人质。

sentences.en: But the images of Palestinian suffering have lately fueled international pressure on Israel to end the war and pushed Western powers to recognize a Palestinian state.
sentences.zh: 但最近巴勒斯坦人受苦的画面加剧了国际社会对以色列结束战争的压力，并推动西方大国承认巴勒斯坦国。

sentences.en: This culminated last week at the United Nations, where a group of world leaders formally recognized Palestinian statehood, which deepened Israel's isolation.
sentences.zh: 上周在联合国，这一趋势达到顶峰，一群世界领导人正式承认了巴勒斯坦的国家地位，这加深了以色列的孤立。

sentences.en: But just a week later, a new peace plan unveiled by President Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu
sentences.zh: 但仅仅一周后，特朗普总统和以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡公布了一项新的和平计划，

sentences.en: underscored the reality that Palestinian statehood is a long way off.
sentences.zh: 强调了一个现实，即巴勒斯坦建国之路还很漫长。

sentences.en: Today, the optimism and the fury of this moment and what this recognition actually means.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将探讨这一时刻的乐观与愤怒，以及这种承认究竟意味着什么。

sentences.en: It's Friday, October 3rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月3日，星期五。

sentences.en: Jess Chung, you are one of the producers on our show.
sentences.zh: 杰斯·钟，你是我们节目的制片人之一。

sentences.en: And last week, you spent time on the ground at the UN to document this historic moment in which the question of Palestinian statehood was really front and center.
sentences.zh: 上周，你亲临联合国现场，记录下了这个历史性时刻，当时巴勒斯坦建国问题确实处于核心位置。

sentences.en: So talk to us a little bit about what you were there to capture.
sentences.zh: 那么，跟我们聊聊你在现场捕捉到了什么。

sentences.en: Well, over the past two years, the international community has grown increasingly frustrated with Israel's tactics in the war.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在过去两年里，国际社会对以色列在战争中的策略越来越感到沮丧。

sentences.en: And what we've seen recently is a push by a number of Western countries like the UK, France, Australia, and Canada
sentences.zh: 我们最近看到的是，英国、法国、澳大利亚和加拿大等一些西方国家正在推动，

sentences.en: to formally recognize the Palestinian state as a way to put pressure on Israel to end the war.
sentences.zh: 正式承认巴勒斯坦国，以此向以色列施压，要求其结束战争。

sentences.en: Now, up until this point, over 140 countries had already done this.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，已经有超过140个国家这样做了。

sentences.en: But what's interesting about this new group of countries is that they're traditionally Israeli allies.
sentences.zh: 但这个新国家群体有趣的地方在于，他们传统上都是以色列的盟友。

sentences.en: That infuriates Israel and the U.S., who say what this is going to do is reward Hamas for its terrorism on October 7th.
sentences.zh: 这激怒了以色列和美国，他们认为这样做是在奖励哈马斯10月7日的恐怖主义行径。

sentences.en: But regardless, 10 countries were planning to come to the U.N.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，有10个国家计划来到联合国。

sentences.en: General Assembly last week to stand up and say for the first time, we recognize the Palestinian state.
sentences.zh: 上周在联合国大会上，他们站出来第一次宣布：我们承认巴勒斯坦国。

sentences.en: So it was going to be a huge moment, and I wanted to capture that.
sentences.zh: 所以这将是一个巨大的时刻，我想记录下来。

sentences.en: — Particularly through the eyes of this one guy, Riyadh Mansour.
sentences.zh: ——特别是通过这个人的视角，利雅得·曼苏尔。

sentences.en: — Okay, we can stand.
sentences.zh: ——好的，我们可以站着。

sentences.en: — Okay.
sentences.zh: ——好的。

sentences.en: — Well, it was a pleasure to meet you.
sentences.zh: ——很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: — Pleasure to meet you.
sentences.zh: ——很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: — Ambassador.
sentences.zh: ——大使。

sentences.en: — Mansour is the Palestinian ambassador to the U.N., and he's worked toward this moment for pretty much his entire life.
sentences.zh: ——曼苏尔是巴勒斯坦驻联合国大使，他几乎一生都在为这一刻而努力。

sentences.en: — We are in the rose garden here at the United Nations.
sentences.zh: ——我们现在在联合国的玫瑰园里。

sentences.en: — Yes.
sentences.zh: ——是的。

sentences.en: — I have beautiful memories here.
sentences.zh: ——我在这里有美好的回忆。

sentences.en: — I meet him in the gardens of the U.N.
sentences.zh: ——我在联合国花园里见到了他，

sentences.en: in midtown Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 位于曼哈顿中城。

sentences.en: This was all before the big meeting was set to take place.
sentences.zh: 这一切都发生在大型会议召开之前。

sentences.en: — He's dressed in a suit.
sentences.zh: ——他穿着西装。

sentences.en: He's got a small Palestinian flag pinned on his lapel.
sentences.zh: 他的翻领上别着一面小小的巴勒斯坦国旗。

sentences.en: — And how long have you been serving in this role?
sentences.zh: ——你担任这个职位多久了？

sentences.en: — In September, 20 years straight.
sentences.zh: ——到九月份，整整20年了。

sentences.en: — 20 years straight.
— Mansour is in his late 70s, and he's been representing Palestinians here for decades.
sentences.zh: ——曼苏尔已经70多岁了，几十年来他一直在这里代表巴勒斯坦人。

sentences.en: — For me, you know, I was working for these things from a long time ago.
sentences.zh: ——对我来说，你知道，我很久以前就开始为这些事情努力了。

sentences.en: — How does it feel to have these countries now on board?
sentences.zh: ——现在有这些国家加入，感觉如何？

sentences.en: — It feels very great.
sentences.zh: ——感觉非常棒。

sentences.en: — We hope from the few days to come that the international community is making a turn.
sentences.zh: ——我们希望在接下来的几天里，国际社会能迎来转折。

sentences.en: — A turn where now having the state of Palestine a reality.
sentences.zh: ——一个让巴勒斯坦国成为现实的转折。

sentences.en: — So we are marching in the direction of peace and justice.
sentences.zh: ——所以我们正朝着和平与正义的方向前进。

sentences.en: — Thank you so much, and I hope to follow you throughout the week.
sentences.zh: ——非常感谢，我希望能在一周内跟进你的行程。

sentences.en: — Okay, very good.
sentences.zh: ——好的，非常好。

sentences.en: — Thank you.
sentences.zh: ——谢谢。

sentences.en: — Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: ——非常感谢。

sentences.en: — Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: ——非常感谢。

sentences.en: We'll touch base.
sentences.zh: 我们保持联系。

sentences.en: — Who are you?
sentences.zh: ——你是谁？

sentences.en: — Because he's been here for so long, Mansour seems to be a kind of fixture in this place.
sentences.zh: ——因为他在这里待了太久，曼苏尔似乎成了这个地方的一种标志性人物。

sentences.en: — He scurries around these halls, doing a seemingly endless amount of press gaggles.
sentences.zh: ——他在这些大厅里匆匆穿梭，进行着似乎无穷无尽的媒体简报。

sentences.en: — Shaking a seemingly endless amount of hands.
sentences.zh: ——握着似乎无穷无尽的手。

sentences.en: — Was she there?
sentences.zh: ——她在那儿吗？

sentences.en: — No, she's over here.
sentences.zh: ——不，她在这一边。

sentences.en: — Meeting a seemingly endless amount of diplomats.
sentences.zh: ——会见着似乎无穷无尽的外交官。

sentences.en: — I'm also a bunch of bullets.
sentences.zh: ——我也有一堆子弹。

sentences.en: — But sitting down with him, I realize that the UN has long been a fixture in his life, too.
sentences.zh: ——但与他坐下来交谈时，我意识到联合国也早已成为他生活的一部分。

sentences.en: — I was born in Palestine, a child of a Palestinian refugee family.
sentences.zh: ——我出生在巴勒斯坦，是一个巴勒斯坦难民家庭的孩子。

sentences.en: — Mansour spent his childhood in Ramallah, in the West Bank.
sentences.zh: ——曼苏尔在约旦河西岸的拉马拉度过了童年。

sentences.en: — And we lived in caves and in the valleys before Onurwa came to the picture.
sentences.zh: ——在近东救济工程处介入之前，我们住在洞穴和山谷里。

sentences.en: — His family was among the hundreds of thousands of Palestinians who were expelled or fled from their homes amid the wars surrounding the creation of the State of Israel in 1948,
sentences.zh: ——他的家人是1948年以色列建国战争期间，数十万被驱逐或逃离家园的巴勒斯坦人之一，

sentences.en: a period known to Palestinians as the Nakba.
sentences.zh: 这段时期被巴勒斯坦人称为“灾难日”。

sentences.en: — And the UN provided food, schools, and medical care to those displaced Palestinian families, including Mansour's.
sentences.zh: ——联合国为那些流离失所的巴勒斯坦家庭（包括曼苏尔的家庭）提供了食物、学校和医疗服务。

sentences.en: — Do you have an early memory about how you understood that Palestinians didn't have a state of your own?
sentences.zh: ——你对了解巴勒斯坦人没有自己的国家有什么早期的记忆吗？

sentences.en: — I don't know exactly what, in those days, the idea of statehood was.
sentences.zh: ——我不知道当时对国家地位的概念到底是什么。

sentences.en: — What was in our mind is we want to return to our towns, to our villages, to our homes.
sentences.zh: ——我们脑子里想的是，我们要回到我们的城镇、我们的村庄、我们的家园。

sentences.en: Like, the key for our house in Palestine, from the town where we were expelled from, was hanging inside the house.
sentences.zh: 就像我们被驱逐出的那个巴勒斯坦城镇的家门钥匙，一直挂在屋里。

sentences.en: So that's a symbol of returning to it.
sentences.zh: 所以那是回归的象征。

sentences.en: — In the 1950s, Mansour's father emigrated to the U.S.
sentences.zh: ——20世纪50年代，曼苏尔的父亲移民到了美国。

sentences.en: — He took a job as a steelworker in Youngstown, Ohio.
sentences.zh: ——他在俄亥俄州的扬斯敦找到了一份钢铁工人的工作。

sentences.en: Mansour was around 17 years old when he followed his father here.
sentences.zh: 曼苏尔大约17岁时跟随父亲来到这里。

sentences.en: He went on to study at Youngstown State.
sentences.zh: 他后来在扬斯敦州立大学学习。

sentences.en: — And I was influenced by the thoughts of the moment.
sentences.zh: ——我受到了当时思想的影响。

sentences.en: — Throughout college, he was politically active, marching for civil rights, against the war in Vietnam, and seeing those movements create real change around him.
sentences.zh: ——在大学期间，他积极投身政治，参加民权游行，反对越南战争，并亲眼见证了这些运动在他周围创造了真正的变革。

sentences.en: — He started speaking out against Israel's occupation in the West Bank, in Gaza, trying to raise awareness of Palestinian rights.
sentences.zh: ——他开始公开反对以色列在约旦河西岸和加沙的占领，试图提高人们对巴勒斯坦权利的认识。

sentences.en: — It wasn't easy.
sentences.zh: ——这并不容易。

sentences.en: It was not popular.
sentences.zh: 这并不受欢迎。

sentences.en: But I was young.
sentences.zh: 但我当时很年轻。

sentences.en: — And then, in 1974, Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat was invited to speak at the U.N.
sentences.zh: ——然后，在1974年，巴勒斯坦领导人亚西尔·阿拉法特首次受邀在联合国发表讲话，

sentences.en: for the first time, where he made an appeal to the international community for a Palestinian state.
sentences.zh: 他在那里向国际社会呼吁建立巴勒斯坦国。

sentences.en: — I was a student, so I brought three buses.
sentences.zh: ——我当时是个学生，所以我带了三辆大巴。

sentences.en: — Mansour organized three buses of people to drive from Ohio to New York for the event.
sentences.zh: ——曼苏尔组织了三辆大巴的人，从俄亥俄州开车到纽约参加这次活动。

sentences.en: — I was among the lucky ones to go to the United Nations to shake hands with Chairman Arafat after he gave his famous speech.
sentences.zh: ——我是幸运儿之一，能去联合国，在阿拉法特主席发表著名演讲后与他握手。

sentences.en: So that was the first time that I entered the U.N.
sentences.zh: 所以那是我第一次进入联合国。

sentences.en: — Palestinians were talking about statehood and what it would mean.
sentences.zh: ——巴勒斯坦人当时在谈论国家地位及其意义。

sentences.en: — Is this what we want?
sentences.zh: ——这是我们想要的吗？

sentences.en: Is it one state, two states?
sentences.zh: 是一个国家，还是两个国家？

sentences.en: — And a decade later, Mansour would take a job at the U.N.
sentences.zh: ——十年后，曼苏尔在联合国找到了一份工作，

sentences.en: and keep pushing for the same goal.
sentences.zh: 并继续为同一个目标奋斗。

sentences.en: — And that journey took a long time, the 80s, the 90s, then the Oslo Agreement.
sentences.zh: ——那段旅程走了很长时间，80年代、90年代，然后是《奥斯陆协议》。

sentences.en: — For years, Mansour worked through cycles of Palestinian intifadas and militancy, Israeli retaliation and expanding settlements,
sentences.zh: ——多年来，曼苏尔经历了巴勒斯坦起义和激进主义、以色列报复和定居点扩张的循环，

sentences.en: new wars, new ceasefires, new peace agreements, like the Oslo Accords, which were seen as the closest to the international community came to resolving the conflict.
sentences.zh: 新的战争、新的停火、新的和平协议，比如《奥斯陆协议》，这被视为国际社会最接近解决冲突的一次尝试。

sentences.en: But in the end, they didn't achieve what they set out to.
sentences.zh: 但最终，它们并没有实现预期的目标。

sentences.en: — You see, we went through cycles.
sentences.zh: ——你看，我们经历了各种循环。

sentences.en: — When Hamas, in a surprise attack, killed 1,200 people and kidnapped about 250 others, pictures emerged of the destroyed kibbutzim,
sentences.zh: ——当哈马斯发动突然袭击，杀害了1200人并绑架了约250人时，被摧毁的基布兹的画面出现了，

sentences.en: videos of hostages being carried away on the backs of motorcycles and trucks driven by militants, stories of people shot in their homes and trapped in burning buildings.
sentences.zh: 人质被武装分子骑着的摩托车和卡车带走的视频，人们在家里被枪杀、被困在燃烧建筑中的故事。

sentences.en: — All of it shocked the world.
sentences.zh: ——这一切震惊了世界。

sentences.en: — There were sympathies in the first few days with the families of the victims as a result of October 7.
sentences.zh: ——在10月7日事件后的最初几天，人们对受害者家属表示了同情。

sentences.en: — But after Israel launched the war against Hamas in Gaza, as that war entered its second year, with more than 60,000 Palestinians dead and the humanitarian situation worsening,
sentences.zh: ——但在以色列对加沙的哈马斯发动战争后，随着战争进入第二年，超过6万巴勒斯坦人死亡，人道主义局势恶化，

sentences.en: people around the world also saw those pictures and heard those stories,
sentences.zh: 世界各地的人们也看到了那些画面，听到了那些故事，

sentences.en: including Mansour, who described what he was seeing in Gaza to the United Nations Security Council this spring.
sentences.zh: 包括曼苏尔，他在今年春天向联合国安理会描述了他在加沙看到的情况。

sentences.en: — The images of mothers embracing their motionless bodies, caressing their hair, talking to them, apologizing to them.
sentences.zh: ——母亲们拥抱着她们冰冷的尸体，抚摸着她们的头发，与她们交谈，向她们道歉的画面。

sentences.en: — It was around that time that Mansour said he felt things begin to shift, and I asked him about that.
sentences.zh: ——就在那时，曼苏尔说他感到事情开始发生转变，我问了他关于这一点。

sentences.en: — It created a tremendous amount of support and empathy and solidarity with the Palestinian people.
sentences.zh: ——这为巴勒斯坦人民赢得了巨大的支持、同情和声援。

sentences.en: — Now the international community, enough is enough.
sentences.zh: ——现在国际社会认为，够了就是够了。

sentences.en: — We're not going to continue going through cycles, up and down, up and down.
sentences.zh: ——我们不会再继续经历这种循环，起起落落，没完没了。

sentences.en: — This time, we're going to stop this war and allow the two-state solution to become a reality.
sentences.zh: ——这一次，我们要停止这场战争，让“两国方案”成为现实。

sentences.en: This is the moment.
sentences.zh: 就是现在。

sentences.en: — C'est pourquoi je déclare que la France reconnaît aujourd'hui l'état de Palestine.
sentences.zh: ——这就是为什么我宣布，法国今天承认巴勒斯坦国。

sentences.en: — I stand before you today, beneath the emblem of the United Nations, to confirm the historic decision of the British government to recognize the state of Palestine.
sentences.zh: ——今天我站在你们面前，在联合国徽章下，确认英国政府承认巴勒斯坦国的历史性决定。

sentences.en: — Portugal formally recognized the state of Palestine.
sentences.zh: ——葡萄牙正式承认巴勒斯坦国。

sentences.en: — A two-state solution.
sentences.zh: ——两国方案。

sentences.en: — Australia recognized the state of Palestine.
sentences.zh: ——澳大利亚承认巴勒斯坦国。

sentences.en: — Canada recognizes the state of Palestine.
sentences.zh: ——加拿大承认巴勒斯坦国。

sentences.en: — Belgium announces the recognition of the state of Palestine.
sentences.zh: ——比利时宣布承认巴勒斯坦国。

sentences.en: — And that is why Ireland last year, with Spain, Norway and Slovenia, recognized the state of Palestine.
sentences.zh: ——这就是为什么爱尔兰去年与西班牙、挪威和斯洛文尼亚一起承认了巴勒斯坦国。

sentences.en: — The systematic decimation of Gaza.
sentences.zh: ——对加沙的系统性摧毁。

sentences.en: — The use of food as a weapon of war.
sentences.zh: ——将食物作为战争武器。

sentences.en: — Children dying of starvation, while food rots at the border.
sentences.zh: ——孩子们死于饥饿，而食物却在边境腐烂。

sentences.en: — The killing of tens of thousands of civilians.
sentences.zh: ——杀害了数万名平民。

sentences.en: — Tens of thousands of civilians.
sentences.zh: ——数万名平民。

sentences.en: — More than 65,000 people killed in Gaza.
sentences.zh: ——加沙有超过65,000人丧生。

sentences.en: — Most of them women and children.
sentences.zh: ——其中大多数是妇女和儿童。

sentences.en: — Horrifically, more than 20,000 of them children.
sentences.zh: ——令人恐惧的是，其中有超过20,000名儿童。

sentences.en: — And hundreds of our own humanitarians.
sentences.zh: ——还有我们数百名自己的人道主义工作者。

sentences.en: — Aid workers.
sentences.zh: ——援助人员。

sentences.en: — Aid workers killed.
sentences.zh: ——援助人员被杀。

sentences.en: — Journalists.
sentences.zh: ——记者。

sentences.en: — Journalists killed.
sentences.zh: ——记者被杀。

sentences.en: — Doctors targeted and killed.
sentences.zh: ——医生被针对并杀害。

sentences.en: — We have reached a point where what has been credibly described as a genocide is being carried out in front of the eyes of the world.
sentences.zh: ——我们已经到了这样一个地步，即被可信地描述为种族灭绝的行为正在全世界的注视下发生。

sentences.en: — Statehood is the inalienable right of the Palestinian people, and that two states is the only path to security and lasting peace for Israelis and Palestinians alike.
sentences.zh: — 建国是巴勒斯坦人民不可剥夺的权利，而“两国方案”是巴勒斯坦人和以色列人实现安全与持久和平的唯一途径。

sentences.en: — Israel denies many of these allegations and strongly refutes the accusation of genocide.
sentences.zh: — 以色列否认了其中许多指控，并强烈驳斥了种族灭绝的罪名。

sentences.en: The Israeli delegation didn't come to the meeting.
sentences.zh: 以色列代表团没有出席这次会议。

sentences.en: Their seats stayed empty.
sentences.zh: 他们的席位空着。

sentences.en: — Today felt so great.
sentences.zh: — 今天感觉真棒。

sentences.en: I think that my tears were coming down on my face.
sentences.zh: 我想我的泪水当时正顺着脸颊流下。

sentences.en: — But Mansour was moved to tears.
sentences.zh: — 但曼苏尔感动得热泪盈眶。

sentences.en: — It's a historic day.
sentences.zh: — 这是一个历史性的日子。

sentences.en: We are climbing a very tall mountain, and we are approaching the top of the mountain.
sentences.zh: 我们正在攀登一座非常高的大山，而且我们已经快要接近山顶了。

sentences.en: — Throughout the week while I was following Mansour, I kept asking him why this moment felt so important.
sentences.zh: — 在我跟踪报道曼苏尔的那一周里，我一直问他为什么这一刻感觉如此重要。

sentences.en: After all, over 140 countries had already recognized Palestine.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，已经有超过140个国家承认了巴勒斯坦。

sentences.en: So isn't this week largely a symbolic gesture?
sentences.zh: 那么，这一周的行动难道不主要是一种象征性的姿态吗？

sentences.en: He kept holding up this analogy.
sentences.zh: 他一直坚持用这个类比。

sentences.en: Apartheid in South Africa.
sentences.zh: 南非的种族隔离制度。

sentences.en: He said much of the world also condemned apartheid for decades.
sentences.zh: 他说，世界上大部分地区几十年来也一直谴责种族隔离制度。

sentences.en: But it was Western countries putting pressure on South Africa that helped end apartheid.
sentences.zh: 但正是西方国家对南非施加的压力，才帮助终结了种族隔离。

sentences.en: So Mansour says he sees this moment as a turning point for statehood.
sentences.zh: 所以曼苏尔说，他将这一刻视为巴勒斯坦建国的转折点。

sentences.en: But this moment has also been controversial.
sentences.zh: 但这一刻也引发了争议。

sentences.en: — What do you say to those who see this recognition as rewarding Hamas for its terrorism?
sentences.zh: — 对于那些认为这种承认是在奖励哈马斯恐怖主义的人，你怎么看？

sentences.en: — I asked Mansour when he thought about the fact that some people view all this formal recognition as a reward to Hamas for the atrocities on October 7th.
sentences.zh: — 我问曼苏尔，当他想到有些人认为所有这些正式承认是对哈马斯10月7日暴行的奖励时，他有何感想。

sentences.en: Mansour told me he thinks that's the wrong way to look at it.
sentences.zh: 曼苏尔告诉我，他认为这种看法是错误的。

sentences.en: — Not only us, but almost all the countries do not agree with that assessment.
sentences.zh: — 不仅是我们，几乎所有国家都不认同这种评估。

sentences.en: Nobody would believe that France, UK, Canada, Australia are rewarding Hamas.
sentences.zh: 没人会相信法国、英国、加拿大和澳大利亚是在奖励哈马斯。

sentences.en: That doesn't make sense.
sentences.zh: 这根本说不通。

sentences.en: All of them, they were doing it as an investment in peace and harmony.
sentences.zh: 他们所有人这样做，都是为了投资于和平与和谐。

sentences.en: — Mansour said Palestinian statehood is not a prize for attacking Israel.
sentences.zh: — 曼苏尔表示，巴勒斯坦建国不是对袭击以色列的奖赏。

sentences.en: He told me it's about the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people to have a state of their own.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，这是关于巴勒斯坦人民拥有自己国家的合法权利。

sentences.en: And that was made clear as the following days unfolded.
sentences.zh: 随着随后几天事态的发展，这一点变得显而易见。

sentences.en: After the break, my colleague Mark Landler on what this recognition means without the support of Israel and the United States.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我的同事马克·兰德勒将为您解读，在没有以色列和美国支持的情况下，这种承认意味着什么。

sentences.en: — I'm Wenna Liu.
sentences.zh: — 我是刘文娜（Wenna Liu）。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的“Connections”谜题。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我热爱恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我还喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: — I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: — 我是萨姆·马祖斯基（Sam Mazursky），我每天负责创作“Spelling Bee”和“Letterboxd”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫“联觉”的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: — New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: — 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像刚才那两位一样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 请访问 nytimes.com/games 开始今天的游戏吧。

sentences.en: — Mark, you have covered this story for decades, the Israel-Palestinian conflict and the fight for Palestinian statehood.
sentences.zh: — 马克，你报道这个故事已经几十年了，关于巴以冲突和巴勒斯坦建国的斗争。

sentences.en: — Yes, I have.
sentences.zh: — 是的，没错。

sentences.en: — Which is why we're turning to you to help us understand what happened not just last week at the UN,
sentences.zh: — 这就是为什么我们要请你来帮助我们理解，不仅是上周在联合国发生了什么，

sentences.en: but also earlier this week when Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited the White House,
sentences.zh: 还有本周早些时候，以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡访问白宫时的情况，

sentences.en: where he stood next to President Trump as President Trump presented this new plan to end the war.
sentences.zh: 当时他站在特朗普总统身边，特朗普总统提出了这个结束战争的新计划。

sentences.en: I want to start with the UN, where the overwhelming support for Palestinian statehood infuriated Netanyahu.
sentences.zh: 我想先从联合国说起，那里对巴勒斯坦建国的压倒性支持激怒了内塔尼亚胡。

sentences.en: Can you walk us through what happened that day?
sentences.zh: 你能带我们回顾一下那天发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: — The assembly will hear an address by His Excellency Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of the State of Israel.
sentences.zh: — 大会将听取以色列国总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡阁下的讲话。

sentences.en: — Well, after these countries stood up and recognized Palestinian statehood,
sentences.zh: — 嗯，在这些国家站出来承认巴勒斯坦建国之后，

sentences.en: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu gave his response.
sentences.zh: 本雅明·内塔尼亚胡总理做出了回应。

sentences.en: — Ladies and gentlemen.
sentences.zh: — 女士们，先生们。

sentences.en: — He took the dais and railed against these moves towards recognition.
sentences.zh: — 他走上讲台，猛烈抨击了这些承认建国的举动。

sentences.en: — This week, the leaders of France, Britain, Australia, Canada, and other countries unconditionally recognized a Palestinian state.
sentences.zh: — 本周，法国、英国、澳大利亚、加拿大和其他国家的领导人无条件地承认了巴勒斯坦国。

sentences.en: They did so after the horrors committed by Hamas on October 7th.
sentences.zh: 他们是在哈马斯于10月7日犯下暴行之后这样做的。

sentences.en: — Netanyahu's argument, in short, is that recognizing Palestinian statehood is a reward for Hamas.
sentences.zh: — 内塔尼亚胡的论点简而言之就是：承认巴勒斯坦建国是对哈马斯的奖励。

sentences.en: — You know what message the leaders who recognized the Palestinian state this week sent to the Palestinians?
sentences.zh: — 你知道本周承认巴勒斯坦国的领导人们向巴勒斯坦人传递了什么信息吗？

sentences.en: It's a very clear message.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常明确的信息。

sentences.en: Murdering Jews pays off.
sentences.zh: 谋杀犹太人是有回报的。

sentences.en: — That what the West is basically saying to Hamas is, you can inflict terror on Israeli citizens, and in our desire for peace,
sentences.zh: — 西方基本上是在对哈马斯说：你们可以对以色列公民施加恐怖，而出于我们对和平的渴望，

sentences.en: we're going to be willing to give you this very symbolic concession.
sentences.zh: 我们愿意给你们这种极具象征意义的让步。

sentences.en: — The Palestinians, they don't believe in this solution.
sentences.zh: — 巴勒斯坦人，他们并不相信这个解决方案。

sentences.en: They never have.
sentences.zh: 他们从来都不信。

sentences.en: They don't want a state next to Israel.
sentences.zh: 他们不想要一个与以色列并存的国家。

sentences.en: They want a Palestinian state instead of Israel.
sentences.zh: 他们想要的是取代以色列的巴勒斯坦国。

sentences.en: — And Netanyahu's argument is what we should really be doing is supporting Israel in its effort to crush Hamas,
sentences.zh: — 而内塔尼亚胡的论点是，我们真正应该做的是支持以色列粉碎哈马斯，

sentences.en: to remove Hamas from the equation altogether, and to back Israel to the hilt, fighting for the return of the hostages and supporting its military campaign in Gaza,
sentences.zh: 将哈马斯彻底从局势中清除，全力支持以色列，为解救人质而战，并支持其在加沙的军事行动，

sentences.en: rather than heading down what he views as this cul-de-sac of recognizing a Palestinian state.
sentences.zh: 而不是走上他所认为的承认巴勒斯坦国这条死胡同。

sentences.en: — I watched Netanyahu's speech, and I was really struck by how many representatives from other countries literally walked out of the hall as he took the stage.
sentences.zh: — 我看了内塔尼亚胡的演讲，令我印象深刻的是，当他走上台时，许多其他国家的代表真的直接走出了大厅。

sentences.en: And yet, despite that, he still had this defiant tone as he talked, which I think really underscored the fact that Israel,
sentences.zh: 然而尽管如此，他在讲话时依然保持着那种挑衅的语调，我认为这确实突显了一个事实：以色列，

sentences.en: even as it's become more and more isolated on the world stage,
sentences.zh: 即使在世界舞台上变得越来越孤立，

sentences.en: Netanyahu has continued to dig his heels in.
sentences.zh: 内塔尼亚胡依然坚持己见。

sentences.en: And that was very evident during his speech at the UN.
sentences.zh: 这一点在他联合国的演讲中表现得非常明显。

sentences.en: — Yes, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: — 是的，我认为你说得对。

sentences.en: And I think he did it for one critical reason.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为他这样做有一个关键原因。

sentences.en: For all those countries that oppose Israel and are critical of Israel, he knows he has one country that is steadfastly behind Israel,
sentences.zh: 对于所有那些反对以色列、批评以色列的国家，他知道他有一个坚定支持以色列的国家，

sentences.en: and that's the United States and particularly President Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 那就是美国，特别是唐纳德·特朗普总统。

sentences.en: He came out against recognition of a Palestinian state.
sentences.zh: 他公开反对承认巴勒斯坦国。

sentences.en: He echoed Netanyahu's argument that this would be a reward for terrorism, a reward for Hamas.
sentences.zh: 他附和了内塔尼亚胡的论点，即这将是对恐怖主义的奖励，是对哈马斯的奖励。

sentences.en: And he did so even as there is some polling that suggests that the American public is far more divided on this issue.
sentences.zh: 尽管有一些民调显示美国公众在这个问题上的分歧要大得多，但他还是这么做了。

sentences.en: After two years of harrowing images of war from Gaza, more Americans are beginning to question unstinting support for the state of Israel, but not the president himself.
sentences.zh: 在经历了两年加沙战争的惨烈画面后，越来越多的美国人开始质疑对以色列国无底线的支持，但总统本人并没有改变立场。

sentences.en: But as long as Trump continues to support Netanyahu, continues to stand behind him in his military campaign in Gaza,
sentences.zh: 但只要特朗普继续支持内塔尼亚胡，继续在他加沙的军事行动中做他的后盾，

sentences.en: I think Netanyahu feels that he has the latitude and the license to be as aggressive as he needs to be.
sentences.zh: 我认为内塔尼亚胡觉得他有足够的余地和许可去采取他认为必要的激进手段。

sentences.en: Obviously, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 显然，美国

sentences.en: is Israel's strongest ally.
sentences.zh: 是以色列最强大的盟友。

sentences.en: But on the question of Palestinian statehood, which of course is what Netanyahu is so angry about, why does the U.S.' position matter so much?
sentences.zh: 但关于巴勒斯坦建国的问题，也就是内塔尼亚胡如此愤怒的原因，为什么美国的立场如此重要？

sentences.en: Well, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 嗯，美国

sentences.en: is so important because it still holds a veto in the United Nations Security Council.
sentences.zh: 之所以如此重要，是因为它在联合国安理会仍然拥有否决权。

sentences.en: So as long as the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以只要美国

sentences.en: is totally behind Israel, there is a limit to what the Palestinians can accomplish.
sentences.zh: 完全支持以色列，巴勒斯坦人所能取得的成就就是有限的。

sentences.en: I think it's also widely understood that without U.S.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们也普遍理解，如果没有美国

sentences.en: buy-in, the whole notion of a two-state solution really falls apart.
sentences.zh: 的参与，整个“两国方案”的概念实际上就会土崩瓦解。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: has always been viewed as the central player in the question of a peace settlement between the Israelis and the Palestinians.
sentences.zh: 一直被视为以色列和巴勒斯坦之间和平协议问题的核心参与者。

sentences.en: That hasn't changed in the last few years, even as these countries have moved toward recognizing Palestine.
sentences.zh: 即使在过去几年里，随着这些国家转向承认巴勒斯坦，这一点也没有改变。

sentences.en: So while it's a very positive step for the Palestinians, without the U.S.
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然这对巴勒斯坦人来说是非常积极的一步，但如果没有美国

sentences.en: joining in, it still has its limits.
sentences.zh: 的加入，它仍然有其局限性。

sentences.en: This is a big, big day, a beautiful day, potentially one of the great days ever in civilization.
sentences.zh: 这是伟大的一天，美好的一天，可能是文明史上最伟大的日子之一。

sentences.en: And so you saw that critical American role on display just this past Monday, when President Trump welcomed Prime Minister Netanyahu back to the White House.
sentences.zh: 所以你看到了美国在关键时刻发挥的作用，就在上周一，特朗普总统欢迎内塔尼亚胡总理重返白宫。

sentences.en: So today is a historic day for peace, and Prime Minister Netanyahu and I have just concluded an important meeting on many vital issues, including...
sentences.zh: 所以今天是和平的历史性一天，内塔尼亚胡总理和我刚刚就许多重要议题结束了一次重要的会晤，包括……

sentences.en: They came out and faced the TV cameras and presented a plan for Gaza, a Trump plan to end the war in Gaza.
sentences.zh: 他们出来面对电视摄像机，提出了一个加沙计划，一个特朗普提出的结束加沙战争的计划。

sentences.en: This proposal calls for the release of all remaining hostages immediately, but in no case more than 72 hours.
sentences.zh: 该提案要求立即释放所有剩余人质，且期限不得超过72小时。

sentences.en: It called on Hamas to give up their weapons, return the hostages immediately.
sentences.zh: 它呼吁哈马斯交出武器，立即归还人质。

sentences.en: They would have no future role in the governance of Gaza.
sentences.zh: 他们在加沙的治理中将不再发挥任何作用。

sentences.en: Israel would remain a very strong military presence around the enclave.
sentences.zh: 以色列将继续在加沙地带周边保持强大的军事存在。

sentences.en: So really very much a pro-Israel plan for Gaza.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是一个非常亲以色列的加沙计划。

sentences.en: With terms that we should note, Hamas has consistently said it would never accept.
sentences.zh: 而且我们应该注意到，哈马斯一贯表示绝不会接受其中的条款。

sentences.en: Absolutely, that Hamas has ruled out unilaterally.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样，哈马斯已经单方面排除了这种可能性。

sentences.en: I should say, though, that our reporting shows many Gazans want Hamas to accept this deal.
sentences.zh: 不过我应该说，我们的报道显示许多加沙人希望哈马斯接受这项协议。

sentences.en: Although a lot of people think it's a real long shot that Hamas ever would.
sentences.zh: 尽管很多人认为哈马斯会接受的可能性微乎其微。

sentences.en: And did this plan say anything explicitly about statehood?
sentences.zh: 那么这个计划是否明确提到了建国问题？

sentences.en: Well, it acknowledged that statehood was an aspiration of the Palestinian people.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它承认建国是巴勒斯坦人民的愿望。

sentences.en: And it suggested that one could envision the creation of a Palestinian state, subject to a number of conditions, including a reform of the Palestinian authority.
sentences.zh: 它暗示可以设想建立一个巴勒斯坦国，但需满足若干条件，包括对巴勒斯坦权力机构进行改革。

sentences.en: I think while we're waiting for signatures and waiting for approvals from a lot of different countries that are involved in this, we probably shouldn't take questions.
sentences.zh: 我想，在我们等待各方签署和批准的同时，我们可能不应该接受提问。

sentences.en: But it left the timeline and the roadmap for all of this completely unclear.
sentences.zh: 但它让这一切的时间表和路线图完全不明朗。

sentences.en: And interestingly, the plan got, in the immediate aftermath, some pretty widespread support among Arab countries, but also among European countries.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，该计划在发布后立即得到了阿拉伯国家以及欧洲国家的广泛支持。

sentences.en: The very countries who, a week earlier, had formally recognized a Palestinian state.
sentences.zh: 而这些国家恰恰在一周前还正式承认了巴勒斯坦国。

sentences.en: What do we make of that, the fact that all these European countries had come out in support of a Palestinian state and now are supporting a plan that seems to heavily favor Israel?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何理解这一点？这些欧洲国家明明都公开支持巴勒斯坦国，现在却支持一个似乎严重偏袒以色列的计划？

sentences.en: I think really what this shows you is the desire among European countries and Arab countries for the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我认为这真正向你展示的是欧洲国家和阿拉伯国家希望美国

sentences.en: to remain engaged in the process.
sentences.zh: 继续参与这一进程的愿望。

sentences.en: I think the mere fact that they saw President Trump stepping forward with a plan, with his name on it,
sentences.zh: 我认为，仅仅是看到特朗普总统站出来提出一个带有他名字的计划，

sentences.en: willing to be heavily engaged and visibly engaged for them was a huge positive.
sentences.zh: 愿意深度参与并公开参与，对他们来说就是一个巨大的积极信号。

sentences.en: I think they feel that they can work out the details, many of which they may not particularly like as the process unfolds.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们觉得随着进程的展开，他们可以解决其中的细节问题，尽管其中许多细节他们可能并不特别喜欢。

sentences.en: But what's vital is for Trump to be involved.
sentences.zh: 但至关重要的是特朗普必须参与其中。

sentences.en: So the image of him standing next to Netanyahu saying he wants to play this role, that was worthy of their support.
sentences.zh: 所以他站在内塔尼亚胡身边说他想发挥这种作用的形象，是值得他们支持的。

sentences.en: And that's why I think he got the kind of show of support that he did.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为他得到了那样的支持表现。

sentences.en: And then immediately after his meeting with President Trump, Prime Minister Netanyahu, speaking to a domestic audience, said in Hebrew,
sentences.zh: 而在与特朗普总统会晤后，内塔尼亚胡总理立即对国内听众用希伯来语说道，

sentences.en: Don't worry, this is never going to happen.
sentences.zh: 别担心，这永远不会发生。

sentences.en: It sort of feels like Netanyahu is kind of talking out of both sides of his mouth, right?
sentences.zh: 这感觉内塔尼亚胡有点两面派，对吧？

sentences.en: Because on the one hand, he gets up at this press conference,
sentences.zh: 因为一方面，他在新闻发布会上站出来，

sentences.en: and he unveils this plan that gives a cursory nod to the possibility of statehood if like 15 unlikely things happen firSt.
sentences.zh: 公布了这个计划，如果先发生15件不可能的事情，它就对建国的可能性点头示意。

sentences.en: And then in Hebrew, he's basically saying, over my dead body.
sentences.zh: 然后用希伯来语，他基本上是在说，除非我死。

sentences.en: And whatever he wants to do, thus far, he's basically had the backing of the United States,
sentences.zh: 无论他想做什么，到目前为止，他基本上都得到了美国的支持，

sentences.en: even as there's been this growing list of countries that say they support Palestinian statehood.
sentences.zh: 尽管越来越多的国家表示支持巴勒斯坦建国。

sentences.en: And so I wonder, where does all of this leave the prospect of a Palestinian state in your mind?
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，在你看来，这一切让巴勒斯坦建国的前景处于什么境地？

sentences.en: Well, you're right to say that Netanyahu was talking out of both sides of his mouth.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你说内塔尼亚胡是两面派是对的。

sentences.en: And one could say, in fact, he's been doing that for many years on this topic.
sentences.zh: 事实上，人们可以说，在这个话题上他多年来一直如此。

sentences.en: If you go back in time, there was a moment when Netanyahu claimed he supported a two-state solution, as did a lot of mainstream Israeli leaders.
sentences.zh: 如果你回顾过去，曾有一段时间内塔尼亚胡声称他支持“两国方案”，许多主流以色列领导人也是如此。

sentences.en: Though it must be said that if you look at Netanyahu's actions over the years, he's really consistently undermined the prospect for a Palestinian state,
sentences.zh: 尽管必须指出，如果你审视内塔尼亚胡多年来的行动，他实际上一直在持续破坏巴勒斯坦建国的前景，

sentences.en: whether it is expanding Jewish settlements in the West Bank or colluding with Hamas in the governance of Gaza, which had the effect of splitting the Palestinian movement in two.
sentences.zh: 无论是扩大西岸的犹太定居点，还是在加沙治理问题上与哈马斯勾结，这都产生了分裂巴勒斯坦运动的效果。

sentences.en: His actions have never been geared toward allowing or encouraging the creation of a Palestinian state.
sentences.zh: 他的行动从来都不是为了允许或鼓励建立巴勒斯坦国。

sentences.en: Now, in some senses, he's being clearer.
sentences.zh: 现在，在某种意义上，他变得更明确了。

sentences.en: He's saying quite publicly that at the moment he thinks a Palestinian state is a dire threat to Israel's security,
sentences.zh: 他公开表示，目前他认为巴勒斯坦国对以色列的安全构成严重威胁，

sentences.en: but he's not willing to completely defy an American president, especially Donald Trump, when he includes this kind of fairly wishy-washy language in his plan for Gaza.
sentences.zh: 但他不愿意完全违抗美国总统，尤其是唐纳德·特朗普，当他在加沙计划中加入这种相当模棱两可的措辞时。

sentences.en: So I think from Netanyahu's point of view, he sees this as something he's simply going to have to live with, and perhaps he's also confident that Hamas will never accept it anyway,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为从内塔尼亚胡的角度来看，他认为这是他不得不忍受的事情，而且也许他也有信心哈马斯永远不会接受它，

sentences.en: so he won't be forced to live with anything that's in this plan anyway.
sentences.zh: 所以他无论如何都不会被迫去接受这个计划中的任何内容。

sentences.en: Mark, our colleague Jess earlier spoke to Riyadh Mansour, the Palestinian ambassador to the UN, and he sounded so optimistic about the real possibility of a Palestinian state.
sentences.zh: 马克，我们的同事杰斯早些时候采访了巴勒斯坦驻联合国大使利雅得·曼苏尔，他听起来对巴勒斯坦建国的现实可能性非常乐观。

sentences.en: And I wonder, just listening to everything that you've outlined, do you think that that optimism is misplaced?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，听了你所概述的一切，你认为这种乐观情绪是否放错了地方？

sentences.en: Well, Riyadh Mansour is looking at this from his particular vantage point, as a diplomat who has spent years, if not decades, lobbying countries to recognize a Palestinian state.
sentences.zh: 嗯，利雅得·曼苏尔是从他特定的角度来看待这个问题的，作为一名外交官，他花费了数年甚至数十年时间游说各国承认巴勒斯坦国。

sentences.en: And in that, he and they have been remarkably successful.
sentences.zh: 在这方面，他和他们取得了显著的成功。

sentences.en: You now have 150-some countries that recognize a Palestinian state, and they include some of the most important and powerful countries in the world.
sentences.zh: 现在有150多个国家承认巴勒斯坦国，其中包括世界上一些最重要和最强大的国家。

sentences.en: So from that point of view, the Palestinians have been remarkably successful.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个角度来看，巴勒斯坦人取得了显著的成功。

sentences.en: But in the nuts and bolts sense of building a state, I think it's a much different story.
sentences.zh: 但从建立国家的具体实务层面来看，我认为情况大不相同。

sentences.en: You have in Gaza a state of war and an enclave that's largely in ruins, where Gaza health officials put the death toll at more than 65,000.
sentences.zh: 加沙目前处于战争状态，且大部分地区已成废墟，加沙卫生官员称死亡人数已超过65,000人。

sentences.en: In the West Bank, you have a territory that's been carved up by the Israelis into an ever-expanding set of Jewish settlements.
sentences.zh: 在约旦河西岸，领土已被以色列人分割成不断扩张的犹太定居点。

sentences.en: You have a Palestinian authority whose control and credibility is in question.
sentences.zh: 巴勒斯坦权力机构的控制力和公信力也备受质疑。

sentences.en: So from the point of view of a viable and functioning state,
sentences.zh: 因此，从建立一个可行且运作良好的国家这一角度来看，

sentences.en: I think the Palestinians are further away from that than they've been for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 我认为巴勒斯坦人距离这一目标比过去很长一段时间都要遥远。

sentences.en: Mark, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 马克，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，雷切尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是您今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: A man rammed a car into a crowd and stabbed people outside of a synagogue in Manchester, England, on Thursday.
sentences.zh: 周四，在英国曼彻斯特，一名男子驾车冲撞人群，并在一家犹太会堂外持刀伤人。

sentences.en: Two people were killed, and three others were seriously injured, in what police called an act of terrorism.
sentences.zh: 警方称这是一起恐怖袭击事件，造成两人死亡，另有三人重伤。

sentences.en: It happened on Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.
sentences.zh: 事发时正值赎罪日，这是犹太历中最神圣的日子。

sentences.en: Police said officers shot and killed the suspect only minutes after he began his assault.
sentences.zh: 警方表示，嫌疑人在开始袭击几分钟后就被赶到的警员击毙。

sentences.en: It is a serious incident, I have to say.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，这是一起严重的事件。

sentences.en: The mayor of Greater Manchester, Andy Burnham, told people to avoid the area where the attack had happened.
sentences.zh: 大曼彻斯特市长安迪·伯纳姆呼吁民众避开袭击发生的区域。

sentences.en: But at the same time, I can give some reassurance immediately to people that the immediate danger appears to be over, and Greater Manchester police have dealt with it very quickly.
sentences.zh: 但同时，我可以立即向民众保证，直接危险似乎已经解除，大曼彻斯特警方处理得非常迅速。

sentences.en: The attacker was identified by Britain's counter-terrorism police as a British citizen of Syrian descent.
sentences.zh: 英国反恐警察确认袭击者是一名叙利亚裔英国公民。

sentences.en: Police said investigators were still working to understand the motive behind the attack.
sentences.zh: 警方表示，调查人员仍在努力查明袭击背后的动机。

sentences.en: And on Friday, officials said that one of the victims had been accidentally shot and killed by an officer who responded to the scene.
sentences.zh: 周五，官员们表示，其中一名受害者是被赶到现场的警员误伤致死的。

sentences.en: And, the Food and Drug Administration approved a generic version of the abortion pill Mifepristone,
sentences.zh: 此外，美国食品药品监督管理局批准了堕胎药米非司酮的仿制药，

sentences.en: making it more easily available at a time when abortion opponents are pressuring the Trump administration to restrict access to abortion pills.
sentences.zh: 在堕胎反对者向特朗普政府施压要求限制堕胎药获取之际，此举使其更容易获得。

sentences.en: The approval, issued earlier this week, means that three American companies can now produce Mifepristone to terminate a pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 本周早些时候发布的这项批准意味着，现在有三家美国公司可以生产用于终止妊娠的米非司酮。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。
